hypothesis: Calling process.stdin.resume() in a spawned child keeps that child alive after the parent exits.
refutedBy: The child is spawned with stdio: "ignore", so its stdin IS /dev/null. resume() starts a read, the read returns EOF immediately, the stream ends, and the ref it was supposed to hold is released in the same tick. The handle exists, so the call succeeds -- it just holds nothing.
witness: A child spawned with stdio: "ignore" and process.stdin.resume() as its only work exits immediately; the same child with an unref'd interval or an open pipe does not.
